This script builds the descriptive tables and exports every table in the analysis to `tables/` as HTML. The exported tables are shown on the [Results](results.qmd) page.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/tables.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/R/tables.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/R/functions.R)
-   [`R/import_clean.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/R/import_clean.R)
-   [`R/modeling.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/R/modeling.R)
-   [`R/pca.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Pirofski-cryptococcus-study/blob/master/R/pca.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/tables.R")
```

## Table 1

Cases and controls are compared on the categorical variables (sex, transplanted organ, race, immunosuppression, CNS disease) and the continuous ones (age and the antibody levels, raw and log). `tbl_summary()` from gtsummary [@sjoberg2021gtsummary] reports medians with interquartile ranges and counts with percentages. `add_p()` uses its defaults: the Wilcoxon rank-sum test for continuous variables, and Fisher's exact or the χ² test for categorical ones, as described in the paper [@yoon2022antibody]. A second version is restricted to participants with antibody measurements.

```{r}
#| label: table-1
#| eval: false
```

## Cryptococcal antigen among cases

Counts of serum cryptococcal antigen results among cases, once as the numeric titer and once as recorded. These are computed for internal checking only and are not exported or published, because they contain small cells.

## Export

Every table is saved as a self-contained HTML file in `tables/`. The gtsummary tables are passed through `relabel_table()` first, so the saved files show readable variable names and categories (for example "Race: White/Black" instead of `RACE` `W`/`B`); the table objects themselves are not changed.

```{r}
#| label: export-tables
#| eval: false
```
